#summary(raw_data)
# ============================================================
# TABLE OF EMPTY CELLS, LITERAL "NAS" VALUES, AND VALID VALUES
# FOR ALL VARIABLES
# ============================================================

missingness_summary <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(raw_data), function(variable) {

    # Temporarily convert to text without modifying the original data frame
    x <- trimws(as.character(raw_data[[variable]]))

    total_n <- length(x)

    # Empty Excel cells are usually imported as NA.
    # This also includes empty strings or values containing only spaces.
    is_empty <- is.na(x) | (!is.na(x) & x == "")

    # Literal "NAS" text, case-insensitive
    is_literal_nas <- !is.na(x) & toupper(x) == "NAS"

    # Values that are neither empty nor "NAS"
    is_valid <- !is_empty & !is_literal_nas

    data.frame(
      variable = variable,

      n_empty = sum(is_empty),
      pct_empty = round(
        100 * sum(is_empty) / total_n,
        2
      ),

      n_literal_nas = sum(is_literal_nas),
      pct_literal_nas = round(
        100 * sum(is_literal_nas) / total_n,
        2
      ),

      n_empty_or_nas = sum(is_empty | is_literal_nas),
      pct_empty_or_nas = round(
        100 * sum(is_empty | is_literal_nas) / total_n,
        2
      ),

      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
)

# Remove row names
rownames(missingness_summary) <- NULL

# Sort from highest to lowest percentage of empty cells plus NAS values
missingness_summary <- missingness_summary[
  order(
    -missingness_summary$pct_empty_or_nas,
    missingness_summary$variable
  ),
]

# Open the complete table in RStudio
View(missingness_summary)

2. Convert numeric variables

##                edad hematocrito_inicial               fr_ph              pto_fr

3. Candidate cohort based on the RETRASCORE paper

The cohort is constructed before the subsequent exclusions based on edad and sdmo. Following the paper, the only exclusion criterion applied here is an unavailable in-hospital mortality outcome. Missing predictor values are retained so they can be described and a complete-case analysis or imputation can be chosen later.

Operationalization decisions:

  • ATLS-based management is a feature of the registry protocol, and no patient-level variable is available for use as a filter.
  • In-hospital mortality combines evolucion_uci and evolucion_hospitalaria, because patients who die in the ICU generally do not have the hospital outcome field completed.
  • The analytical outcome is mortality_30d: deaths within 30 days of trauma are coded as 1; live hospital discharges and deaths after day 30 are coded as 0. Deceased patients without a valid date retain an unknown outcome.
  • triss_death_probability is calculated as 1 - ps/100, because ps is stored as a survival percentage ranging from 0 to 100.
  • Medical prehospital care is defined as uvi movil or helicoptero; the categories no medicalizada, sin atencion prehospitalaria, and soporte vital enfermeria form the reference group.
  • Hemodynamic failure is approximated by shock or shock refractario in situacion_hemodinamica; respiratory failure is defined as PaO2/FiO2 less than or equal to 200 in adrs.
  • situacion_hemodinamica, adrs, coagulopatia, vmec_dico, and hemorragia_masiva are assumed to represent the first 24 hours, as defined in the registry. The export has no timestamp that allows this to be verified for each patient.
  • mais1-mais6 are used directly according to the current code mapping. In these fields, 0, an empty cell, NA, na, or NAS all mean that no lesion is present in that anatomical region and are therefore coded as 0.
# Helper functions ---------------------------------------------------------

clean_text <- function(x) {
  x <- tolower(trimws(as.character(x)))
  x[x %in% c("", "na", "nas")] <- NA_character_
  x
}

clean_number <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  x[x %in% c("", "NA", "NAS")] <- NA_character_
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", x)))
}

# In-hospital outcome. Patients who die in the ICU generally have an empty
# hospital outcome, so both outcome fields are combined.
clean_icu_outcome <- clean_text(raw_data$evolucion_uci)
clean_hospital_outcome <- clean_text(raw_data$evolucion_hospitalaria)

in_hospital_mortality <- case_when(
  clean_icu_outcome %in% c("exitus", "exitus y donacion") ~ 1L,
  clean_hospital_outcome %in% c(
    "exitus", "exitus y donacion"
  ) ~ 1L,
  clean_hospital_outcome == "alta" ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

# Primary outcome from the paper: mortality within 30 days of trauma.
# fecha_alta_uci is used for ICU deaths and fecha_alta_hospital for deaths
# after ICU discharge. fecha_exitus is used as a fallback.
icu_death <- clean_icu_outcome %in% c(
  "exitus", "exitus y donacion"
)
hospital_death <- clean_hospital_outcome %in% c(
  "exitus", "exitus y donacion"
)

death_date <- as.POSIXct(
  rep(NA_real_, nrow(raw_data)),
  origin = "1970-01-01",
  tz = "UTC"
)
death_date[icu_death] <- raw_data$fecha_alta_uci[icu_death]
death_date[hospital_death] <- raw_data$fecha_alta_hospital[
  hospital_death
]

use_recorded_death_date <- in_hospital_mortality == 1 &
  is.na(death_date) & !is.na(raw_data$fecha_exitus)
use_recorded_death_date[is.na(use_recorded_death_date)] <- FALSE
death_date[use_recorded_death_date] <- raw_data$fecha_exitus[use_recorded_death_date]

days_to_death <- as.numeric(
  difftime(death_date, raw_data$fecha_trauma, units = "days")
)
valid_death_date <- !is.na(days_to_death) & days_to_death >= 0

# Survival beyond day 30 is considered 30-day survival even if the patient
# dies later; these later deaths are not excluded.
mortality_30d <- case_when(
  in_hospital_mortality == 0 ~ 0L,
  in_hospital_mortality == 1 &
    valid_death_date & days_to_death <= 30 ~ 1L,
  in_hospital_mortality == 1 &
    valid_death_date & days_to_death > 30 ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

# Comparators used in the paper.
icu_length_of_stay_days <- clean_number(raw_data$dias_uci)
triss_survival_pct <- clean_number(raw_data$ps)
triss_death_probability <- ifelse(
  !is.na(triss_survival_pct) & triss_survival_pct >= 0 & triss_survival_pct <= 100,
  1 - triss_survival_pct / 100,
  NA_real_
)

# Patient-related variables -----------------------------------------------

clean_sex <- clean_text(raw_data$genero)
male <- case_when(
  clean_sex == "masculino" ~ 1L,
  clean_sex == "femenino" ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

age <- clean_number(raw_data$edad)
age_category <- cut(
  age,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 49, 65, 75, Inf),
  labels = c("<50", "50-65", "66-75", ">75"),
  right = TRUE
)

clean_antiplatelet <- clean_text(raw_data$antiagregado)
clean_vka <- clean_text(raw_data$dicumarinicos)
clean_doac <- clean_text(raw_data$acod)

preinjury_antithrombotic <- case_when(
  clean_antiplatelet == "si" |
    clean_vka == "si" |
    clean_doac == "si" ~ 1L,
  clean_antiplatelet == "no" &
    clean_vka == "no" &
    clean_doac == "no" ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

# Prehospital variables ----------------------------------------------------

clean_prehospital_care <- clean_text(raw_data$atencion_prehospitalaria)
physician_prehospital_care <- case_when(
  clean_prehospital_care %in% c("uvi movil", "helicoptero") ~ 1L,
  clean_prehospital_care %in% c(
    "no medicalizada", "sin atencion prehospitalaria",
    "soporte vital enfermeria"
  ) ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

clean_prehospital_intubation <- clean_text(raw_data$iot_prehospitalaria)
prehospital_intubation <- case_when(
  clean_prehospital_intubation %in% c(
    "si", "si, con empleo de dispositivos de apoyo"
  ) ~ 1L,
  clean_prehospital_intubation == "no" ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

clean_trauma_type <- clean_text(raw_data$tipo_trauma)
penetrating_trauma <- case_when(
  clean_trauma_type == "penetrante" ~ 1L,
  clean_trauma_type == "contuso" ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

clean_mechanism <- clean_text(raw_data$mecanismo)
# Requested grouping: other and unknown form a single category.
# Empty values remain NA and are not included in this category.
clean_mechanism[clean_mechanism %in% c(
  "otro", "otros", "desconocido"
)] <- "otros/desconocido"
clean_intent <- clean_text(raw_data$intencionalidad)

injury_type <- factor(
  case_when(
    clean_intent == "no intencional : trafico" ~
      "Road Traffic accident",
    clean_intent == "no intencional : caida" ~ "Fall",
    clean_intent == "no intencional : laboral" ~
      "Occupational accident",
    clean_intent == "no intencional : deportivo" ~
      "Sport related",
    clean_intent == "intencionado : agresion" ~ "Assault",
    clean_intent == "intencionado : autolisis" ~ "Self-injury",
    clean_intent == "desconocido" ~ "Unknown",
    clean_intent == "no intencional : otras actividades" ~
      "Other",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ),
  levels = c(
    "Road Traffic accident", "Fall", "Occupational accident",
    "Sport related", "Assault", "Self-injury", "Unknown", "Other"
  )
)

# Every patient whose intent is self-injury (autolysis) is high risk, whatever
# the actual mechanism of the injury.
high_risk_mechanism <- case_when(
  clean_intent == "intencionado : autolisis" ~ 1L,
  clean_mechanism %in% c(
    "arma de fuego", "atropello", "caida accidental", "otros/desconocido"
  ) ~ 1L,
  !is.na(clean_mechanism) & clean_mechanism != "precipitacion" ~ 0L,
  clean_mechanism == "precipitacion" &
    !is.na(clean_intent) ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

# Self-injury as an independent binary variable (1 = self-injury, 0 = any other
# recorded intentionality, including unknown intentionality, which is not
# documented as self-injury). Empty intentionality remains missing.
self_injury <- case_when(
  clean_intent == "intencionado : autolisis" ~ 1L,
  !is.na(clean_intent) ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

# Physiological variables --------------------------------------------------

clean_pupils <- clean_text(raw_data$pupilas_ingreso)
pupil_category <- factor(
  case_when(
    clean_pupils == "sin alteraciones" ~ "normal",
    clean_pupils == "midriasis unilateral" ~ "midriasis unilateral",
    clean_pupils == "midriasis bilatera" ~ "midriasis bilateral",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ),
  levels = c("normal", "midriasis unilateral", "midriasis bilateral")
)

gcs_total <- clean_number(raw_data$gcs_total_introducido)
gcs_le_8 <- ifelse(
  is.na(gcs_total), NA_integer_, as.integer(gcs_total <= 8)
)

# Anatomical variables -----------------------------------------------------
# RETRAUCI regional MAIS variables are used directly:
# mais1 head, mais2 upper extremity, mais3 thorax, mais4 abdomen,
# mais5 lower extremity (including pelvis; see the pelvis split below), and
# mais6 external/thermal injuries.
# In this export, 0, an empty MAIS cell, NA, na, and NAS all mean that no injury
# is present in that region and are coded as 0. Other non-numeric values or
# values outside the AIS 0-6 range are retained as missing.

convert_regional_mais <- function(x) {
  text_value <- trimws(as.character(x))
  is_empty <- is.na(text_value) | text_value == "" |
    toupper(text_value) %in% c("NA", "NAS")
  result <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", text_value)))
  result[is_empty] <- 0
  result[!is.na(result) & !(result %in% 0:6)] <- NA_real_
  result
}

dichotomize_mais <- function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), NA_integer_, as.integer(x >= 3))
}

# Severity of each anatomical region as a Yes/No variable: "Yes" when the
# regional AIS is 4 or higher, "No" when it is 3 or lower (including 0 = no
# injury in the region). "No" is the reference category.
categorize_mais <- function(x) {
  factor(
    case_when(
      is.na(x) ~ NA_character_,
      x >= 4 ~ "Yes",
      x <= 3 ~ "No"
    ),
    levels = c("No", "Yes")
  )
}

# Regional AIS values -------------------------------------------------------

head_ais <- convert_regional_mais(raw_data$mais1)
upper_extremity_ais <- convert_regional_mais(raw_data$mais2)
thorax_ais <- convert_regional_mais(raw_data$mais3)
abdomen_ais <- convert_regional_mais(raw_data$mais4)
lower_extremity_incl_pelvis_ais <- convert_regional_mais(raw_data$mais5)
external_ais <- convert_regional_mais(raw_data$mais6)

# Pelvis and lower extremity are analysed separately. In the AIS 2005 coding
# used by the registry, region 8 (lower extremity) includes the pelvis. Pelvic
# lesions are those whose AIS code (lesion_X_ais) starts with 8561 (pelvic ring)
# or 8562 (acetabulum). The text in lesion_X_nombre is a generic menu label and
# is NOT used to identify the pelvis.
# - pelvis_ais: maximum AIS severity among pelvic lesions (0 if none).
# - lower_extremity_ais: maximum AIS severity among the remaining region-8
#   lesions (pelvis excluded).
# Patients with no region-8 lesion detail in lesion_X_* cannot be split, so for
# them the total lower-extremity MAIS (mais5) is kept as lower extremity and
# pelvis_ais is 0. Their number is reported in the summary table below.
lesion_indices <- 0:31
lesion_region_columns <- paste0("lesion_", lesion_indices, "_region_ais")
lesion_severity_columns <- paste0("lesion_", lesion_indices, "_gravedad")
lesion_code_columns <- paste0("lesion_", lesion_indices, "_ais")

missing_lesion_columns <- setdiff(
  c(lesion_region_columns, lesion_severity_columns, lesion_code_columns),
  names(raw_data)
)
if (length(missing_lesion_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Missing lesion columns: ",
    paste(missing_lesion_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

lesion_region <- sapply(raw_data[lesion_region_columns], clean_number)
lesion_severity <- sapply(raw_data[lesion_severity_columns], clean_number)
lesion_code_prefix <- sapply(
  raw_data[lesion_code_columns],
  function(x) substr(trimws(as.character(x)), 1, 4)
)
lesion_severity[!(lesion_severity %in% 1:6)] <- NA_real_

is_lower_limb_lesion <- lesion_region == 8
is_lower_limb_lesion[is.na(is_lower_limb_lesion)] <- FALSE
is_pelvic_lesion <- is_lower_limb_lesion &
  matrix(
    lesion_code_prefix %in% c("8561", "8562"),
    nrow = nrow(lesion_code_prefix)
  )
is_nonpelvic_lower_limb_lesion <- is_lower_limb_lesion & !is_pelvic_lesion

max_lesion_severity <- function(selected_lesions) {
  severity <- ifelse(selected_lesions, lesion_severity, 0)
  result <- apply(severity, 1, max, na.rm = TRUE)
  # A selected lesion without a valid severity leaves the maximum unknown.
  result[rowSums(selected_lesions & is.na(lesion_severity)) > 0] <- NA_real_
  result
}

has_lower_limb_detail <- rowSums(is_lower_limb_lesion) > 0
pelvis_ais <- max_lesion_severity(is_pelvic_lesion)
lower_extremity_ais <- ifelse(
  has_lower_limb_detail,
  max_lesion_severity(is_nonpelvic_lower_limb_lesion),
  lower_extremity_incl_pelvis_ais
)

# Organ failures within the first 24 hours --------------------------------

clean_hemodynamic_status <- clean_text(raw_data$situacion_hemodinamica)
hemodynamic_failure <- case_when(
  clean_hemodynamic_status %in% c("shock", "shock refractario") ~ 1L,
  clean_hemodynamic_status %in% c(
    "estable", "inestable remonta con volumen"
  ) ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

clean_respiratory_status <- clean_text(raw_data$adrs)
respiratory_failure <- case_when(
  clean_respiratory_status %in% c("<100", "101-200") ~ 1L,
  clean_respiratory_status %in% c("no", "201 -300", "> 300") ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

clean_coagulopathy <- clean_text(raw_data$coagulopatia)
coagulopathy_24h <- case_when(
  clean_coagulopathy == "si" ~ 1L,
  clean_coagulopathy == "no" ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

# Treatments within the first 24 hours ------------------------------------

clean_mechanical_ventilation <- clean_text(raw_data$vmec_dico)
mechanical_ventilation <- case_when(
  clean_mechanical_ventilation == "si" ~ 1L,
  clean_mechanical_ventilation == "no" ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

clean_massive_hemorrhage <- clean_text(raw_data$hemorragia_masiva)
massive_hemorrhage <- case_when(
  clean_massive_hemorrhage == "si" ~ 1L,
  clean_massive_hemorrhage == "no" ~ 0L,
  TRUE ~ NA_integer_
)

# Final cohort -------------------------------------------------------------

retrascore_cohort <- data.frame(
  row_id = seq_len(nrow(raw_data)),
  medical_record = raw_data$historia,
  registry_record = raw_data$registro,
  hospital = raw_data$hospital,
  trauma_year = year(raw_data$fecha_trauma),
  in_hospital_mortality = in_hospital_mortality,
  mortality_30d = mortality_30d,
  days_to_death = days_to_death,
  icu_length_of_stay_days = icu_length_of_stay_days,
  triss_death_probability = triss_death_probability,
  male = male,
  age = age,
  age_category = age_category,
  preinjury_antithrombotic = preinjury_antithrombotic,
  physician_prehospital_care = physician_prehospital_care,
  prehospital_intubation = prehospital_intubation,
  penetrating_trauma = penetrating_trauma,
  injury_type = injury_type,
  grouped_mechanism = clean_mechanism,
  high_risk_mechanism = high_risk_mechanism,
  self_injury = self_injury,
  pupils = pupil_category,
  gcs_total = gcs_total,
  gcs_le_8 = gcs_le_8,
  head_ais = head_ais,
  head_mais = dichotomize_mais(head_ais),
  head_mais_group = categorize_mais(head_ais),
  thorax_ais = thorax_ais,
  thorax_mais = dichotomize_mais(thorax_ais),
  thorax_mais_group = categorize_mais(thorax_ais),
  abdomen_ais = abdomen_ais,
  abdomen_mais = dichotomize_mais(abdomen_ais),
  abdomen_mais_group = categorize_mais(abdomen_ais),
  upper_extremity_ais = upper_extremity_ais,
  upper_extremity_mais = dichotomize_mais(upper_extremity_ais),
  upper_extremity_mais_group = categorize_mais(upper_extremity_ais),
  lower_extremity_incl_pelvis_ais = lower_extremity_incl_pelvis_ais,
  lower_extremity_incl_pelvis_mais_group = categorize_mais(lower_extremity_incl_pelvis_ais),
  lower_extremity_ais = lower_extremity_ais,
  lower_extremity_mais = dichotomize_mais(lower_extremity_ais),
  pelvis_ais = pelvis_ais,
  pelvis_mais = dichotomize_mais(pelvis_ais),
  external_ais = external_ais,
  external_mais = dichotomize_mais(external_ais),
  external_mais_group = categorize_mais(external_ais),
  hemodynamic_failure = hemodynamic_failure,
  respiratory_failure = respiratory_failure,
  coagulopathy_24h = coagulopathy_24h,
  mechanical_ventilation = mechanical_ventilation,
  massive_hemorrhage = massive_hemorrhage
)

initial_n <- nrow(retrascore_cohort)
unknown_outcome_n <- sum(
  is.na(retrascore_cohort$in_hospital_mortality)
)

retrascore_cohort <- retrascore_cohort %>%
  filter(!is.na(in_hospital_mortality))

cohort_flow <- data.frame(
  stage = c(
    "Initial records",
    "Excluded: unknown in-hospital mortality",
    "RETRASCORE cohort"
  ),
  n = c(initial_n, unknown_outcome_n, nrow(retrascore_cohort))
)

    sum(is.na(x))

  pct_missing = round(vapply(retrascore_cohort, function(x) {
    100 * mean(is.na(x))
  }, numeric(1)), 2),
  row.names = NULL
)

The table shows, for the final cohort, how many patients have a severe injury (AIS >= 3) in each group and how many patients lack lesion-level detail in region 8, for whom the pelvic and non-pelvic components cannot be separated.

Preprocessed cohort

The preprocessed data remain available in memory as the retrascore_cohort object. This document does not write an RDS file or any other data file.

Logistic regression with a temporal split

The model uses the same 13 predictors included in the final logistic regression from the previous study. Complete cases are split temporally by year of trauma: patients injured in 2020-2023 form the training set and patients injured in 2024-2025 form the validation set. The model is fitted only in the training set. Patients injured outside 2020-2025 (or without a valid trauma date) are not used.

# Variables retained in the previous study.
selected_predictors <- c(
  "age_category",
  "preinjury_antithrombotic",
  "prehospital_intubation",
  "high_risk_mechanism",
  "pupils",
  "gcs_le_8",
  "head_mais",
  "thorax_mais",
  "hemodynamic_failure",
  "respiratory_failure",
  "coagulopathy_24h",
  "mechanical_ventilation",
  "massive_hemorrhage"
)

outcome_variable <- "mortality_30d"
required_variables <- c(outcome_variable, selected_predictors)
model_variables <- c("row_id", "trauma_year", required_variables)
missing_variables <- setdiff(required_variables, names(retrascore_cohort))

if (length(missing_variables) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "The following model variables are missing: ",
    paste(missing_variables, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Logistic regression uses complete cases for the outcome and all predictors.
complete_case_rows <- complete.cases(
  retrascore_cohort[, required_variables, drop = FALSE]
)
model_data <- droplevels(
  retrascore_cohort[complete_case_rows, model_variables, drop = FALSE]
)

if (nrow(model_data) == 0L) {
  stop("No complete cases are available for model fitting.")
}
if (!identical(sort(unique(model_data[[outcome_variable]])), c(0L, 1L))) {
  stop("The model outcome must contain both 0 and 1.")
}

# Temporal split by year of trauma: train 2020-2023, validate 2024-2025.
training_years <- 2020:2023
validation_years <- 2024:2025

training_data <- model_data[
  model_data$trauma_year %in% training_years,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
test_data <- model_data[
  model_data$trauma_year %in% validation_years,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

if (nrow(training_data) == 0L || nrow(test_data) == 0L) {
  stop("The training or validation period contains no complete cases.")
}
for (split_data in list(training_data, test_data)) {
  if (!identical(sort(unique(split_data[[outcome_variable]])), c(0L, 1L))) {
    stop("Each temporal sample must contain both outcome classes.")
  }
}

model_formula <- reformulate(
  termlabels = selected_predictors,
  response = outcome_variable
)

logistic_model <- glm(
  formula = model_formula,
  data = training_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  na.action = na.fail
)

if (!isTRUE(logistic_model$converged)) {
  stop("The logistic regression did not converge.")
}
if (anyNA(coef(logistic_model))) {
  stop("The logistic regression contains non-estimable coefficients.")
}

Data-driven variable selection

The following analyses do not use the predictors retained by the previous study as prior information. The three methods (LASSO, elastic net and stepwise AIC) start from the same set of 17 eligible clinical candidate predictors. Anatomical injury severity enters through all six regions (head, upper extremity, thorax, abdomen, lower extremity including pelvis, and external), each as a Yes/No variable (regional AIS >= 4 = Yes, AIS <= 3 = No). A variable is selected when it is retained. Identifiers, year, other outcomes, variables measured after the outcome, and the TRISS prediction are excluded.

Variable selection is performed exclusively in the 2020-2023 training period defined for the first logistic regression. Patients with complete data for all 17 candidates are assigned to the training (2020-2023) or validation (2024-2025) period by year of trauma. The 2024-2025 validation sample is not used for variable selection or model estimation.

required_selection_packages <- c("glmnet", "MASS", "pROC")
missing_selection_packages <- required_selection_packages[
  !vapply(
    required_selection_packages,
    requireNamespace,
    logical(1),
    quietly = TRUE
  )
]

if (length(missing_selection_packages) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Install the following packages before running variable selection: ",
    paste(missing_selection_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# All eligible predictors are offered to both selection methods without
# assigning priority to any variable.
candidate_predictors <- c(
  # Non-anatomical predictors of the original study
  "age_category",
  "preinjury_antithrombotic",
  "prehospital_intubation",
  "high_risk_mechanism",
  "self_injury",
  "pupils",
  "gcs_le_8",
  "hemodynamic_failure",
  "respiratory_failure",
  "coagulopathy_24h",
  "mechanical_ventilation",
  "massive_hemorrhage",
  # The six anatomical regions (mais1-mais6), each as Yes (AIS >= 4) / No
  "head_mais_group",
  "upper_extremity_mais_group",
  "thorax_mais_group",
  "abdomen_mais_group",
  "lower_extremity_incl_pelvis_mais_group",
  "external_mais_group"
)

selection_variables <- c(
  "row_id", "trauma_year", outcome_variable, candidate_predictors
)
missing_candidate_variables <- setdiff(
  selection_variables,
  names(retrascore_cohort)
)

if (length(missing_candidate_variables) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "The following candidate variables are missing: ",
    paste(missing_candidate_variables, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

selection_complete_rows <- complete.cases(
  retrascore_cohort[, selection_variables, drop = FALSE]
)
selection_data <- droplevels(
  retrascore_cohort[
    selection_complete_rows,
    selection_variables,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
)

if (nrow(selection_data) == 0L) {
  stop("No complete cases are available for variable selection.")
}

# Assign patients to the temporal training and validation periods.
selection_training_data <- selection_data[
  selection_data$trauma_year %in% training_years,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
selection_test_data <- selection_data[
  selection_data$trauma_year %in% validation_years,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

if (nrow(selection_training_data) == 0L || nrow(selection_test_data) == 0L) {
  stop("The training or validation period contains no selection cases.")
}

selection_formula <- reformulate(
  termlabels = candidate_predictors,
  response = outcome_variable
)

LASSO selection

LASSO selection uses ten outcome-stratified cross-validation folds in the training sample. Predictors are standardized by glmnet, and the conservative lambda.1se value determines the selected model. A categorical predictor is considered selected when at least one of its indicator coefficients is nonzero.

training_design_matrix_full <- model.matrix(
  selection_formula,
  data = selection_training_data
)
training_design_matrix <- training_design_matrix_full[, -1, drop = FALSE]
training_outcome <- selection_training_data[[outcome_variable]]

design_assignment <- attr(training_design_matrix_full, "assign")[-1]
selection_term_labels <- attr(terms(selection_formula), "term.labels")

set.seed(20261028)
number_of_folds <- 10L
fold_id <- integer(length(training_outcome))

for (outcome_level in sort(unique(training_outcome))) {
  level_indices <- which(training_outcome == outcome_level)
  fold_id[level_indices] <- sample(rep(
    seq_len(number_of_folds),
    length.out = length(level_indices)
  ))
}

lasso_cv_model <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(
  x = training_design_matrix,
  y = training_outcome,
  family = "binomial",
  alpha = 1,
  foldid = fold_id,
  type.measure = "deviance",
  standardize = TRUE
)

lasso_coefficients <- as.numeric(
  coef(lasso_cv_model, s = "lambda.1se")[-1, 1]
)
names(lasso_coefficients) <- colnames(training_design_matrix)

lasso_term_strength <- vapply(
  seq_along(selection_term_labels),
  function(term_index) {
    max(abs(lasso_coefficients[design_assignment == term_index]))
  },
  numeric(1)
)
names(lasso_term_strength) <- selection_term_labels

lasso_selected_predictors <- names(lasso_term_strength)[
  lasso_term_strength > 0
]

Elastic net selection

Elastic net combines the L1 (LASSO) and L2 (ridge) penalties, which makes selection more stable when predictors are correlated (for example, the MAIS scores of several body regions). The mixing parameter alpha is tuned together with lambda: for each alpha in the grid below, glmnet::cv.glmnet is run with the same ten outcome-stratified folds used for LASSO, and the alpha with the lowest cross-validated deviance is retained (alpha = 1 is the LASSO already fitted above, so the grid covers only 0.1-0.9). For the chosen alpha, the conservative lambda.1se value determines the selected model, as in LASSO. A categorical predictor is considered selected when at least one of its indicator coefficients is nonzero.

elastic_net_alpha_grid <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1)

elastic_net_cv_models <- lapply(
  elastic_net_alpha_grid,
  function(alpha_value) {
    glmnet::cv.glmnet(
      x = training_design_matrix,
      y = training_outcome,
      family = "binomial",
      alpha = alpha_value,
      foldid = fold_id,
      type.measure = "deviance",
      standardize = TRUE
    )
  }
)

elastic_net_alpha_table <- data.frame(
  Alpha = elastic_net_alpha_grid,
  `Lambda (1se)` = vapply(
    elastic_net_cv_models, function(m) m$lambda.1se, numeric(1)
  ),
  `Minimum CV deviance` = vapply(
    elastic_net_cv_models, function(m) min(m$cvm), numeric(1)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

best_alpha_index <- which.min(elastic_net_alpha_table$`Minimum CV deviance`)
elastic_net_alpha <- elastic_net_alpha_grid[best_alpha_index]
elastic_net_cv_model <- elastic_net_cv_models[[best_alpha_index]]

elastic_net_coefficients <- as.numeric(
  coef(elastic_net_cv_model, s = "lambda.1se")[-1, 1]
)
names(elastic_net_coefficients) <- colnames(training_design_matrix)

elastic_net_term_strength <- vapply(
  seq_along(selection_term_labels),
  function(term_index) {
    max(abs(elastic_net_coefficients[design_assignment == term_index]))
  },
  numeric(1)
)
names(elastic_net_term_strength) <- selection_term_labels

elastic_net_selected_predictors <- names(elastic_net_term_strength)[
  elastic_net_term_strength > 0
]

elastic_net_alpha_table[c("Lambda (1se)", "Minimum CV deviance")] <- lapply(
  elastic_net_alpha_table[c("Lambda (1se)", "Minimum CV deviance")],
  round,
  digits = 5
)

Alpha Lambda (1se) Minimum CV deviance

Stepwise selection

Bidirectional stepwise selection starts from the full 17-predictor logistic model and minimizes Akaike’s information criterion (AIC). It uses the same training patients as LASSO and elastic net.

full_selection_model <- glm(
  formula = selection_formula,
  data = selection_training_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  na.action = na.fail
)

if (!isTRUE(full_selection_model$converged)) {
  stop("The full model used for stepwise selection did not converge.")
}

stepwise_model <- MASS::stepAIC(
  full_selection_model,
  direction = "both",
  trace = FALSE
)

if (!isTRUE(stepwise_model$converged)) {
  stop("The stepwise logistic regression did not converge.")
}

stepwise_selected_predictors <- attr(
  terms(stepwise_model),
  "term.labels"
)

Logistic models using the selected variables

The selection methods determine the predictor sets only. Three standard, unpenalized multivariable logistic regressions are then fitted in the same 2020-2023 training sample: one using the variables selected by LASSO, one using those selected by elastic net and one using those selected by stepwise AIC.

lasso_refit_formula <- reformulate(
  termlabels = lasso_selected_predictors,
  response = outcome_variable
)
elastic_net_refit_formula <- reformulate(
  termlabels = elastic_net_selected_predictors,
  response = outcome_variable
)
stepwise_refit_formula <- reformulate(
  termlabels = stepwise_selected_predictors,
  response = outcome_variable
)

lasso_refit_model <- glm(
  formula = lasso_refit_formula,
  data = selection_training_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  na.action = na.fail
)
elastic_net_refit_model <- glm(
  formula = elastic_net_refit_formula,
  data = selection_training_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  na.action = na.fail
)
stepwise_refit_model <- glm(
  formula = stepwise_refit_formula,
  data = selection_training_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  na.action = na.fail
)

if (!isTRUE(lasso_refit_model$converged) || anyNA(coef(lasso_refit_model))) {
  stop("The logistic model using LASSO-selected variables is not estimable.")
}
if (!isTRUE(elastic_net_refit_model$converged) || anyNA(coef(elastic_net_refit_model))) {
  stop("The logistic model using elastic-net-selected variables is not estimable.")
}
if (!isTRUE(stepwise_refit_model$converged) || anyNA(coef(stepwise_refit_model))) {
  stop("The logistic model using stepwise-selected variables is not estimable.")
}

Training and test AUC of the refitted logistic models

Predictions use the three unpenalized logistic models refitted after variable selection. Performance is reported both in the 2020-2023 training sample and in the 2024-2025 validation sample (patients with complete data for all candidate predictors). The validation AUC therefore measures temporal discrimination in patients who were not used for variable selection or coefficient estimation. AUC 95% confidence intervals are calculated with DeLong’s method.

Interaction model: head x abdomen

The logistic model fitted with the variables selected by stepwise AIC is compared with an otherwise identical model that adds one interaction term between anatomical regions: head x abdomen (each region coded Yes if AIS >= 4 and No if AIS <= 3). If a region of the interaction was not selected by stepwise AIC, its main effect is added together with the interaction. All models are fitted in the 2020-2023 training sample and evaluated in the 2024-2025 validation sample. The likelihood-ratio test compares the interaction model with the stepwise model without interaction; the DeLong test compares the validation AUC of the interaction model with that of the stepwise model (paired, same patients).

Models restricted to significant predictors

The refitted models above can retain predictors whose coefficients are not statistically significant. Here, each of the three logistic models is simplified by backward elimination in the 2020-2023 training sample: the predictor with the highest likelihood-ratio p value (drop1, chi-squared test, evaluated per variable so that all categories of a factor are kept or removed together) is removed, the model is refitted, and the process is repeated until every remaining predictor has p < 0.05. Each anatomical region is therefore kept as a Yes/No variable (AIS >= 4 vs <= 3) if it is significant. The 2024-2025 validation sample is not used.

significance_threshold <- 0.05

eliminate_nonsignificant_predictors <- function(model, threshold) {
  removed_predictors <- character(0)
  repeat {
    term_tests <- drop1(model, test = "Chisq")
    term_tests <- term_tests[rownames(term_tests) != "<none>", , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(term_tests) == 0L) break
    p_values <- term_tests[["Pr(>Chi)"]]
    worst_index <- which.max(p_values)
    if (p_values[worst_index] < threshold) break
    removed_term <- rownames(term_tests)[worst_index]
    removed_predictors <- c(removed_predictors, removed_term)
    model <- update(model, as.formula(paste(". ~ . -", removed_term)))
  }
  list(model = model, removed = removed_predictors)
}

lasso_significant <- eliminate_nonsignificant_predictors(
  lasso_refit_model, significance_threshold
)
elastic_net_significant <- eliminate_nonsignificant_predictors(
  elastic_net_refit_model, significance_threshold
)
stepwise_significant <- eliminate_nonsignificant_predictors(
  stepwise_refit_model, significance_threshold
)

lasso_significant_model <- lasso_significant$model
elastic_net_significant_model <- elastic_net_significant$model
stepwise_significant_model <- stepwise_significant$model

Effect of adding self-injury to the model

self_injury is an independent binary variable (1 = self-injury intent). Every patient with self-injury intent is also coded as high_risk_mechanism = 1, whatever the mechanism, so self_injury is a subset of high_risk_mechanism. It is offered as a candidate predictor in the variable selection above. This section compares three versions of the final model: without high_risk_mechanism, with it, and with high_risk_mechanism plus self_injury. The models are fitted in the training sample (2020-2023) and the validation sample (2024-2025) is used only to evaluate them.

new3 <- glm(
  formula = mortality_30d ~ age_category + preinjury_antithrombotic +
    prehospital_intubation + pupils + gcs_le_8 + hemodynamic_failure +
    respiratory_failure + coagulopathy_24h + mechanical_ventilation +
    massive_hemorrhage + head_mais_group + high_risk_mechanism +
    self_injury + external_mais_group,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  data = selection_training_data,
  na.action = na.fail
)

Mortality by score: model with the first LASSO variables

This section converts the logistic model fitted with the variables selected by the first LASSO (lasso_refit_model, training sample 2020-2023) into a points score, in the style of the RETRASCORE figure. Each coefficient is divided by log_odds_per_point (1 point = 0.5 log-odds) and rounded to the nearest integer, keeping at least 1 point for every retained term; the score of a patient is the sum of the points of the risk factors present. The bars show the observed 30-day mortality for each score value (scores of score_cap_high or more are pooled in the last bar), the dotted line is a second-degree polynomial trend line, and the table below the bars gives the score, the observed mortality (%) and the number of patients. The colours are the risk groups, defined with the same mortality bands as in the original figure applied to the observed mortality of the training sample, so that a score has the same colour in both figures.

library(ggplot2)
## Warning: package 'ggplot2' was built under R version 4.5.3
# ---- Points of the RETRASCORE-style score -----------------------------------
# 1 point = `log_odds_per_point` log-odds of the logistic model fitted with the
# LASSO-selected variables. Every coefficient is divided by this value and
# rounded; each retained term keeps at least 1 point (in absolute value).
log_odds_per_point <- 0.5
score_cap_high <- 17L          # scores >= this value (i.e. > 16) are pooled in one bar

score_model <- lasso_refit_model
score_coefficients <- coef(score_model)[-1]
score_points <- sign(score_coefficients) *
  pmax(1, round(abs(score_coefficients) / log_odds_per_point))

score_points_table <- data.frame(
  Term = names(score_points),
  Coefficient = round(unname(score_coefficients), 3),
  Points = unname(score_points),
  row.names = NULL
)
knitr::kable(
  score_points_table,
  align = c("l", "r", "r"),
  caption = paste0(
    "Points of the score derived from the logistic model with the ",
    "LASSO-selected variables (1 point = ", log_odds_per_point, " log-odds)"
  )
)

massive_hemorrhage 1.073 2
head_mais_groupYes 1.491 3
external_mais_groupYes 2.612 5 
patient_score <- function(data) {
  design <- model.matrix(
    delete.response(terms(score_model)),
    data = data, xlev = score_model$xlevels
  )[, names(score_points), drop = FALSE]
  as.numeric(design %*% score_points)
}

score_by_value <- function(data) {
  score <- pmin(patient_score(data), score_cap_high)
  out <- aggregate(
    data[[outcome_variable]], by = list(score = score),
    FUN = function(x) c(n = length(x), deaths = sum(x))
  )
  out <- data.frame(score = out$score, out$x)
  out$mortality <- 100 * out$deaths / out$n
  out
}

training_score_table <- score_by_value(selection_training_data)
validation_score_table <- score_by_value(selection_test_data)

# Risk groups: same bands as the RETRASCORE figure, applied to the observed
# 30-day mortality of the TRAINING sample (made monotone with cummax) so that a
# given score has the same colour in the training and the validation figure.
risk_group_labels <- c(
  "Very low (< 5 %)", "Low (5-<20 %)", "Medium (20-<40 %)",
  "High (40-<70 %)", "Very high (70-<85 %)", "Extreme (>= 85 %)"
)
risk_group_colours <- c(
  "#4e8a3e", "#fbe8b1", "#ffd966", "#c55a11", "#e8372c", "#c00000"
)
names(risk_group_colours) <- risk_group_labels

score_range <- seq(
  min(training_score_table$score, validation_score_table$score),
  score_cap_high
)
training_rate <- training_score_table$mortality[
  match(score_range, training_score_table$score)
]
training_rate[is.na(training_rate)] <- 0
training_rate <- cummax(training_rate)
score_group <- cut(
  training_rate, breaks = c(-Inf, 5, 20, 40, 70, 85, Inf), right = FALSE,
  labels = risk_group_labels
)
names(score_group) <- score_range

plot_score_mortality <- function(score_table, sample_label,
                                 model_label = "the LASSO-selected variables",
                                 left_expand = 3.8) {
  d <- merge(
    data.frame(score = score_range), score_table, by = "score", all.x = TRUE
  )
  d$n[is.na(d$n)] <- 0
  d$mortality[is.na(d$mortality)] <- 0
  d$group <- score_group[as.character(d$score)]
  d$pct_label <- ifelse(
    d$n == 0, "-", ifelse(d$mortality < 10, sprintf("%.1f", d$mortality),
                          sprintf("%.0f", d$mortality))
  )
  d$score_label <- ifelse(
    d$score == score_cap_high, paste0(">", score_cap_high - 1L), d$score
  )
  x_first <- min(d$score)

  # Dotted polynomial (degree 2) trend line of the bars, as in the original
  # figure; only the part between 0 and 100 % is drawn.
  fit <- lm(mortality ~ poly(score, 2), data = d[d$n > 0, ])
  trend <- data.frame(score = seq(min(d$score), max(d$score), length.out = 200))
  trend$fitted <- predict(fit, newdata = trend)
  trend <- trend[trend$fitted >= 0 & trend$fitted <= 100, ]

  ggplot(d, aes(x = score, y = mortality)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = group), width = 0.6) +
    geom_line(
      data = trend, aes(x = score, y = fitted), inherit.aes = FALSE,
      colour = "#2a78d6", linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.9
    ) +
    # Data table under the bars: score, % mortality and n
    geom_tile(aes(y = -6), width = 1, height = 5.5, fill = "white",
              colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_tile(aes(y = -12), width = 1, height = 5.5, fill = "white",
              colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_tile(aes(y = -18), width = 1, height = 5.5, fill = "white",
              colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(aes(y = -6, label = score_label), size = 3.1, fontface = "bold") +
    geom_text(aes(y = -12, label = pct_label), size = 2.9) +
    geom_text(aes(y = -18, label = n), size = 2.7, colour = "grey30") +
    annotate("text", x = x_first - 0.75, y = c(-6, -12, -18), hjust = 1,
             label = c("Score", "Mortality %", "n"), size = 3.1,
             fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = risk_group_colours, drop = FALSE,
                      name = "Risk group") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = expansion(add = c(left_expand, 0.7))) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq(0, 100, 10), limits = c(-21, 100), expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "30-day mortality by score",
      subtitle = paste0(
        sample_label, ". Score from the logistic model with ",
        model_label, " (1 point = ", log_odds_per_point, " log-odds)."
      ),
      x = NULL, y = "Mortality %"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "top",
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
}

Risk groups (derivation sample)

risk_group_fill <- c(
  "Very low" = "#A9D18E", "Low" = "#FFF2CC", "Medium" = "#FFD966",
  "High" = "#BF9000", "Very high" = "#FF0000", "Extreme" = "#FF0000"
)

# One row per risk group, for the derivation (training) sample.
risk_group_summary <- function(score_table) {
  d <- merge(
    data.frame(score = score_range, group = score_group[as.character(score_range)]),
    score_table, by = "score", all.x = TRUE
  )
  d$n[is.na(d$n)] <- 0
  d$deaths[is.na(d$deaths)] <- 0
  groups <- levels(droplevels(d$group))
  rows <- lapply(groups, function(g) {
    x <- d[d$group == g, ]
    seen <- x[x$n > 0, ]
    data.frame(
      group = g,
      points_min = min(x$score), points_max = max(x$score),
      n = sum(x$n), deaths = sum(x$deaths),
      risk_min = min(seen$mortality), risk_max = max(seen$mortality)
    )
  })
  out <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  out$pooled <- 100 * out$deaths / out$n
  out
}

# Table in the style of the RETRASCORE risk-group table (Points, % risk, Groups)
plot_risk_table <- function(score_table, model_label, show_title = TRUE,
                            fixed_ends = FALSE) {
  s <- risk_group_summary(score_table)
  k <- nrow(s)
  fmt <- function(x) ifelse(x < 10, sprintf("%.1f", x), sprintf("%.0f", x))
  s$points_label <- ifelse(
    s$points_min == s$points_max, s$points_min,
    paste(s$points_min, "-", s$points_max)
  )
  if (k > 1) {
    s$points_label[1] <- paste("<", s$points_min[2])
    s$points_label[k] <- paste(">", s$points_max[k - 1])
  }
  s$risk_label <- ifelse(
    s$risk_min == s$risk_max, paste0(fmt(s$risk_min), " %"),
    paste0(fmt(s$risk_min), " - ", fmt(s$risk_max), " %")
  )
  if (fixed_ends) {
    s$risk_label[1] <- "< 5 %"
    s$risk_label[k] <- "> 85 %"
  }
  s$group_name <- toupper(sub(" \\(.*$", "", s$group))
  s$fill <- risk_group_fill[sub(" \\(.*$", "", s$group)]
  s$row <- k - seq_len(k)          # first group at the top

  col_x <- c(0, 1.4, 3.2, 5.2)
  cells <- rbind(
    data.frame(col = 1, row = k, label = "POINTS", fill = "white", bold = TRUE),
    data.frame(col = 2, row = k, label = "% RISK", fill = "white", bold = TRUE),
    data.frame(col = 3, row = k, label = "GROUPS", fill = "white", bold = TRUE),
    data.frame(col = 1, row = s$row, label = s$points_label, fill = "white", bold = TRUE),
    data.frame(col = 2, row = s$row, label = s$risk_label, fill = s$fill, bold = FALSE),
    data.frame(col = 3, row = s$row, label = s$group_name, fill = "white", bold = FALSE)
  )
  cells$xmin <- col_x[cells$col]
  cells$xmax <- col_x[cells$col + 1]

  title_labs <- if (show_title) {
    labs(
      title = "Risk groups of the score (derivation sample, 2020-2023)",
      subtitle = paste0("Score from the logistic model with ", model_label,
                        ".\n% risk = range of the observed 30-day mortality",
                        " of the score values in each group.")
    )
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  ggplot(cells) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = row, ymax = row + 1,
                  fill = fill), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = row + 0.5, label = label,
                  fontface = ifelse(bold, "bold", "plain")), size = 6) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    title_labs +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9), plot.margin = margin(8, 12, 8, 12))
}
plot_risk_table(training_score_table, "the LASSO-selected variables")

Mortality by score: same model without the external MAIS

Same analysis as above, but the logistic model is refitted without external_mais_group (the remaining variables selected by the first LASSO are kept). The points are recalculated from the new coefficients with the same rule (1 point = log_odds_per_point log-odds, rounded, at least 1 point per term), and the risk-group colours are again defined from the observed mortality of the training sample.

no_external_predictors <- setdiff(lasso_selected_predictors, "external_mais_group")

score_model <- glm(
  formula = reformulate(no_external_predictors, response = outcome_variable),
  data = selection_training_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  na.action = na.fail
)
if (!isTRUE(score_model$converged) || anyNA(coef(score_model))) {
  stop("The logistic model without the external MAIS is not estimable.")
}

score_coefficients <- coef(score_model)[-1]
score_points <- sign(score_coefficients) *
  pmax(1, round(abs(score_coefficients) / log_odds_per_point))

score_points_table <- data.frame(
  Term = names(score_points),
  Coefficient = round(unname(score_coefficients), 3),
  Points = unname(score_points),
  row.names = NULL
)

    "Points of the score derived from the logistic model with the ",
    "LASSO-selected variables except the external MAIS (1 point = ",
    log_odds_per_point, " log-odds)"
  )
)
